brief.summary: Stocks bounced (S&P futures +0.9%, Nasdaq +1%) after the Fed's first hike in three years; the long end led a relief rally, the 30-year down about 3bp near 5.33% and the 2-year off 2bp to 4.71%, flattening the curve. Brent fell roughly 2% toward $100 on a partial Saudi pipeline restart, while the dollar firmed toward 155 yen. Warsh was hawkish and orthodox—removing accommodation, inflation too high, economy strengthening—with 16 of 18 dots seeing more hikes; markets price 53% odds of an October hike and roughly 75% for December. Credit stayed placid and tech led gains, though banks flagged soft trading. Geopolitics and pullback risk temper the tone; net mildly risk-on.
notable_quotes: This is the beginning of a rate hike cycle.
I would be hard pressed to describe broad financial conditions as restrictive.
